## Why Each Piece Is Here

### `from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware`
`fastapi/middleware/cors.py` is a one-liner re-export:
```python
# fastapi/middleware/cors.py
from starlette.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware as CORSMiddleware  # noqa
```
This is the stable FastAPI-blessed import path (not `starlette.middleware.cors` directly).

### `app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...)` — **before routes**
`FastAPI.build_middleware_stack()` in `fastapi/applications.py` assembles the stack as:
```
ServerErrorMiddleware
  → [your user_middleware, in reverse registration order]   ← CORSMiddleware lands here
    → ExceptionMiddleware
      → AsyncExitStackMiddleware
        → Router (your routes)
```
`add_middleware()` **appends** to `user_middleware`, so calling it before routes ensures it is in the stack before any request reaches a route handler. CORS preflight `OPTIONS` requests are intercepted and short-circuited at the middleware layer — they never reach your route functions.

### Parameter choices

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `allow_origins` | explicit list | Only the two local dev origins are trusted — never use `["*"]` with `allow_credentials=True` |
| `allow_credentials` | `True` | Allows the browser to send cookies and `Authorization` headers cross-origin |
| `allow_methods` | `["*"]` | Permits all HTTP methods; narrow this (e.g. `["GET","POST"]`) for stricter APIs |
| `allow_headers` | `["*"]` | Reflects any request header back; narrow to e.g. `["Content-Type","Authorization"]` for stricter APIs |

> ⚠️ **Security note:** `allow_origins=["*"]` and `allow_credentials=True` together are **invalid** per the CORS spec and Starlette will raise a `ValueError`. Always use an explicit origins list when credentials are enabled.
